solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: However made, a TV programme easy to dip in and out of

indicators.text: to dip in and out of
indicators.note: dipping in and out of a word means touching one letter, skipping the next, touching the one after

parts.note: the article as printed
a situation comedy

parts.words: easy to dip in and out of
parts.note: E and S, the first and third letters of EaSy

explanation.surface: A TV guide praising a show you can watch any episode of without losing the thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'However made' reads like the start of a TV review, but it is the definition: an order taken 'as it comes' is accepted however it happens to be made.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from ordering drinks: whisky or coffee 'as it comes' is served however it is made, with no special instructions.

clue.text: It sets like a shot

parts.note: as = like
a pic is a photo, a shot

explanation.surface: Something that sets instantly, quick as a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a shot' is an idiom for 'instantly', so the surface says the thing sets fast; the solver has to break the idiom into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: aspic is a savoury jelly, and setting is what jelly does.

clue.text: Finally hotel-resistant, staggering around end of tour

indicators.note: someone staggering lurches about unsteadily, as these letters do out of their order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of touR, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A tourist ending a tour by staggering about, finally refusing to go back to the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram needs one more letter than 'hotel-resistant' supplies; the R from the end of 'tour' is the letter the others stagger around.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'in the last resort' means when all else has failed, so finally.

clue.text: Herald's lying in grass with a collection of books

parts.note: couch grass, a creeping weed
the article as printed
NT = New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A herald lounging on the lawn with a pile of books.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface the apostrophe-s means 'is'; for the definition it is possessive: the herald's word for 'lying'.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: in heraldry, a beast shown lying down with its head raised is described as couchant.

clue.text: Egotist's urgent claim that spreads online

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that spreads online'

parts.note: the egotist's favourite word, about themself
the same word said again, urgently, to claim attention

explanation.surface: A self-obsessed person's demands going viral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me! Me!' is the egotist's urgent cry. 'Claim' does double duty, as the egotist's demand and as the kind of assertion that gets passed around the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by behaviour: a meme is an image, joke or idea that users copy and pass on until it has spread across the internet.

clue.text: Boor reacts furiously — language!

indicators.note: a furious reaction flails wildly, throwing the letters out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A lout loses his temper, and someone scolds him for his swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language!' is what you snap at someone swearing, so it hides as a reprimand rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Serbo-Croat is the South Slavic language spoken in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro.

clue.text: Carried on getting regular money

definitions.meaning: as in carried on a war or a campaign

explanation.surface: Someone kept going because a salary kept coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: One word doing two jobs: a past-tense verb (to wage war) and an adjective (the waged, as against the unwaged).
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain synonyms: to wage a war is to carry it on, and the waged are those drawing a regular pay packet.

clue.text: Exhausted fiancée stops scheming like some women

indicators.note: something exhausted has been emptied out, so the word keeps only its shell of outer letters

parts.note: wily = cunning, scheming

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it

parts.note: FiancéE with its middle emptied out

explanation.surface: A worn-out bride-to-be gives up her plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'stops' mean 'gives up'; it is the plugging sense. The accent on fiancée is irrelevant, since only its first and last letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: wifely means befitting a wife, and wives are some women.

clue.text: Dropping arms, she strangely exhibits small attention span

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are in an odd, unfamiliar order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: A woman lets her arms fall and seems unable to concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a verb acting on 'arms', as if letters were to be removed; it is simply fodder, and every letter of the first three words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a grasshopper mind jumps from topic to topic like the insect, which is a short attention span.

clue.text: Splitting up, speak rudely to individual not working

parts.note: to dis someone is to speak disrespectfully of them
PERSONAL (individual) without ON

explanation.surface: A couple breaking up, one insulting the other for being out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speak rudely to' reads as one verb phrase; the 'to' is only glue. The deletion takes ON out of the middle of PERSONAL, not off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: a crowd's splitting up and scattering is its dispersal.

clue.text: Novel way to prepare extending the patio?

definitions.meaning: the surface reads 'new'; the setter means a book, a novel

definitions.text: way to prepare extending the patio?
definitions.meaning: flags are paving flagstones, not banners: laying more of them makes a patio bigger

explanation.surface: A new method for getting ready to enlarge a garden terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Put Out More Flags is Evelyn Waugh's 1942 novel. Read literally, its title is an instruction to lay more paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The title's words, taken at face value, describe setting out extra flagstones, which is how you extend a patio.

clue.text: Babies here in playground wearing red

definitions.note: a place clued by what is found there

indicators.note: a garment being worn wraps round its wearer

parts.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal red revolutionary
the rec, short for recreation ground

explanation.surface: Toddlers in a playground dressed in red.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the playground wearing red; the wordplay puts the red round the playground. 'Red' looks like a colour but is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by contents: a crèche is a nursery, the place where babies are looked after.

clue.text: Two sources of energy containing key blend

indicators.note: to contain something is to hold it inside

parts.note: COAL, and E, the physics symbol for energy
the Esc key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A mix of two power sources, with something key in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' wants to be an adjective or a musical key; it is the escape key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: things that coalesce blend and merge into one.

clue.text: Don't go near ox, plainly

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
clear as an adverb, as in 'loud and clear'

explanation.surface: A plain warning to keep away from an ox.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a farmyard warning that means exactly what the answer means, so the definition hardly hides.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from navigation: to steer clear of something is to keep well away from it.

clue.text: Her actions damaged one of several branches

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, as these letters are

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: Someone's behaviour broke off part of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests a tree her actions harmed; they are shops of one retailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by relation: each outlet of a retail chain is one branch among many.

clue.text: Pale actor transformed her death scene?

definitions.note: the answer is the queen; the definition names her by her most famous scene

indicators.note: to transform something is to change its form, here the order of the letters

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A pallid actress changing for her big death scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an indirect definition: 'her' is the woman whose death by asp bite is among the most famous on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: the asp-bite suicide ending Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra is her death scene.

clue.text: School leaving German castle in deficit

indicators.note: to leave a place is to go out of it

parts.note: Schloss is German for castle
sch is the standard abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A school pulls out of a German castle trip that ran at a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Even without German, the abbreviation SCH for school shows where the deletion starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from accounts: a business running at a loss is in deficit.

clue.text: Cooking Italian brought up to eat with old men

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up lifts it from bottom to top, so the word reads upwards
what eats takes the food inside it

parts.note: It. is the abbreviation for Italian
and = with
O = old
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An Italian chef invited to dinner with a group of old men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' looks like what the Italian is doing; it is the definition, as in a style of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: tandoori is a style of Indian cooking done in a clay oven, the tandoor.

clue.text: Takes on board chairs, not the first

indicators.note: the word is taken without its first letter, which is not included

parts.note: seats = chairs

explanation.surface: A board meeting where the one who takes the chair is not the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes on board' suggests understanding an idea; here it is food being taken on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokey idiom: taking food on board means eating it.

clue.text: Visited a fellow motoring enthusiast to give a bit of a hand

parts.note: met = visited, as in met with
the article as printed
a PAL (fellow) whose passion is the CAR

explanation.surface: Dropping in on a fellow car enthusiast to help out with some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a hand' promises help; the definition is literally a part of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by part: the metacarpals are the five bones of the palm, each a bit of the hand.

clue.text: Leg after end of swim, one still glowing

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
coming after means following in order

parts.note: last letter of swiM
an ember is a piece of a dying fire still glowing

explanation.surface: A swimmer's leg, still glowing after the final length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' does not mean the leg comes after the swim; it tells you the glowing piece follows the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a leg is a limb, and member is a formal word for a limb.

clue.text: Authoritative impression of reserve with a little money around

indicators.note: something placed around another surrounds it

parts.note: a few pence is a small sum
res is the abbreviation for reserve

explanation.surface: A reserved person who gives an impression of authority despite having little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a personality trait belonging with 'impression'; it is only the abbreviation RES.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular sense: someone with presence makes a commanding impression just by being in the room.

clue.text: Bother sailors beginning to swab decks

parts.note: ado = fuss, bother
RN = Royal Navy

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Swab

explanation.surface: Sailors are made to begin swabbing the ship's decks.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'sailors' and 'swab' around it, 'decks' reads as the floors of a ship; it is the verb, as in 'deck the halls'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to deck a room with holly is to adorn it.

clue.text: Source of sweetness in sauces from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means starting at the bottom and reading upwards

parts.note: ragus, Italian meat sauces

explanation.surface: Looking for what makes Southern cooking sauces so sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the south' sounds like regional cooking, but in a down clue it says the word runs bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: sugar is the everyday ingredient added to make food sweet.

clue.text: Fancy wife being supported by that man

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is supported rests on top

parts.note: w = wife
him = that man

explanation.surface: A wife likes the idea of being kept by her man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb (the wife fancies being kept); it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: a passing fancy is a sudden, idle notion.

clue.text: Sorting out problems with noise in parliament?

parts.note: troubles = problems
a parliament is the collective noun for owls, and this is the noise they make

explanation.surface: Dealing with the problem of rowdy MPs shouting in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' wants to be Westminster; the question mark hints at a parliament of owls. 'Problems' belongs to the wordplay, although 'sorting out problems' reads as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular sense: troubleshooting is tracing and sorting out faults, especially in machines or systems.

clue.text: A prison is busy

parts.note: the article as printed
stir is old slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail is a hive of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a complete sentence; the definition is its last word and 'is' joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both adjectives: a household astir is up and moving about, busy.

clue.text: Several weeks in Provence introduced to provide rest

parts.note: to render a service is to provide it
Mai is French for May, a month of several weeks

explanation.surface: A few weeks in the south of France as a well-earned break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Provence' means 'in French', so the several weeks are a French month; 'rest' looks like a holiday and means what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: the rest of something is what is left, its remainder.
